_: The register of terms tmct coins or borrows that name a concept from a discipline.
One row per term: the area it belongs to, the verdict from archive/PLAN_NORMATIVE.md, and the
authoritative source it traces to. Checked by `node scripts/term-inventory.mjs --register`:
every term must still occur in the tree, so a row cannot outlive the code it describes.
A term earns a row when it names a discipline's concept. `idx`, `rows` and `tail` do not.
verdict: aligned | map | extend | rename | drop | open
probe:   the literal string to look for; defaults to the term itself

terms.cite: de Kleer, "An Assumption-based TMS", Artificial Intelligence 28(2), 1986, pp. 127-162, DOI 10.1016/0004-3702(86)90080-9, s4.2 p. 143. NOT Doyle: "A Truth Maintenance System", AI 12(3), 1979, pp. 231-272
terms.note: tmct's (mgx:factJustification premise ids + mgx:sourceRule) is an ATMS justification - antecedents, consequent, informant - which de Kleer describes as Horn clauses, monotonic by construction. A JTMS justification is (SL inlist outlist) and the OUTLIST is what makes it an assumption; tmct has none, ever. de Kleer names the real gap: tmct stores justifications and computes no labels. NB Reiter 1980 never uses the word "justification" at all.

terms.note: the element is a (triple, source) RECORD, not a triple: core.mjs files every assertion under <groupId>@<sourceId> and unions provenance tags inside it. So it is a G-Set of records each carrying a G-Set of tags, plus a per-source revision chain that demotes rather than deletes. PLAN_MUD_WEBRTC.md's "a G-Set's merge rule, byte for byte" is right about union and loose about granularity.

terms.cite: Shapiro et al., INRIA RR-7687, Definition 2.3 (eventual consistency plus strong convergence: replicas that delivered the same updates have equivalent state)

terms.cite: Shapiro et al., INRIA RR-7506, s3.2.1, Specifications 8-9 (LWW-Register), attributing it to Johnson & Thomas, RFC 677, "The Maintenance of Duplicate Databases", 1975-01-27
terms.note: tmct's latest-wins is a READ-time query (adventure.mjs's foldWorldState ranks by (epoch, turn); rulingTestimonyClaim by epoch/firsthand/turn/gone), never a merge-time register - the loser stays in the store so its citation stays readable. NB RR-7506's own bibliography misdates RFC 677 as January 1976; the RFC is dated 27 January 1975.

terms.cite: Shapiro et al., INRIA RR-7506, s3.3.2 (2P-Set) and s3.3.5 (OR-Set)
terms.note: the only tombstone tmct has is compaction's: assertionGroupsFor refuses a source a pool-1 rollup already absorbed, so an absorbed assertion is not resurrected by the next sync. Retraction (removeFacts) writes no tombstone and does not replicate, so a retracted fact returns from any peer that still holds it.

terms.cite: Hellerstein, "The Declarative Imperative: Experiences and Conjectures in Distributed Logic", ACM SIGMOD Record 39(1), 2010, pp. 5-19, DOI 10.1145/1860702.1860704 (conjecture); Ameloot, Neven, Van den Bussche, "Relational Transducers for Declarative Networking", PODS 2011 pp. 283-292 and JACM 60(2) Art. 15, 2013, DOI 10.1145/2450142.2450151 (proof); Hellerstein & Alvaro, "Keeping CALM", CACM 63(9), 2020, pp. 72-81, DOI 10.1145/3369736
terms.note: the base layer is monotone and coordination-free, so CALM applies to it. The read is NOT: ranking rows and taking the newest means "there is no later row", which is negation. Moving it to the read buys CONFLUENCE (same set, same view), not monotonicity - and only because p2p-room.mjs sorts Fact individuals by content-addressed id so the fold is a function of the set. Hellerstein's paper is 2010, commonly misdated 2011.
